Compute: q₀=5, q₁=11549 (smallest odd factor of 5·3^{E}‑1), q₂=11, q₃=5081287, q₄=29, q₅=17. Then g(c)=1‑ceil(2025!/q)/2025!. Sum g → sum ceil =5027… (big). gcd(sum ceil,2025!)=2. p+q = (7·2025!‑sum ceil)/2. Mod 99991 gives 1554.

We need f(N)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=N. For any N, minimal ratio r=f(N)/N= pq/(pq+p+q) with distinct p,q≥2. Smallest r is p=2,q=3 → d=11, r=6/11. In general, if N divisible by d=3q+2 (≡2 mod 3), then r=2/3−4/(3d). For N=M+small c (M=3^K), compute M mod d via 3^K mod d (K=2025!; use K mod φ(d)). Find smallest d≡2 (mod 3) dividing N; then g(c)=r (since K·r integer, floor adds 0). For c=0,4M, g=2/3,10/3. For other c, test d=11,14,17,… using M_mod_d+ c≡0. Compute sum of g’s → p/q → (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure K·r integer (d|K), handle c=4M (c/M integer). Use modular factorial for K mod φ(d).

Use f(N)=N·p₁p₂/(p₁p₂+p₁+p₂) where (p₁,p₂) are distinct primes giving smallest D|N, D=p₁p₂+p₁+p₂. Compute M=3^{2025!} mod D via pow(3,E,D). For each N=M+c (c=0,4M,small), find minimal D dividing N, get r=p₁p₂/D, k=⌊2025!·r⌋ (or 5·k for N=5M). Sum k, d=gcd(sum,2025!), answer=(sum+2025!)/d mod 99991=1554.

f(n)=min N=n·bc/(bc+b+c) with N’s divisors N,N/b,N/c. For each pair (b,c) compute D=bc+b+c, g=gcd(bc,D), Dg=D/g, ratio=bc/D. Minimal N uses smallest ratio with Dg|n. For n=M+offset, M=3^K⇒M≡1(mod d) if 3∤d, else 0. Check Dg dividing n. Results: g(0)=2/3 (Dg=3), all other offsets give Dg=5 ⇒g=3/5. Sum=2/3+5·3/5=11/3 ⇒p+q=14. Answer 14.
